spec_features.spec_quote: A few defaults are set to reduce gratuitous induced distress
spec_features.evidence: config.py:91-102 defines humane_stop=True, debrief_after_rollout=True, give_up honoring, and turn_budgets['extended']=12; all are read and acted on in run.py (run_cell passes them to run_rollout) and harness.run_rollout enforces them. The collection of defaults genuinely changes execution toward less prolonged distress.
spec_features.notes: This is an umbrella for the concrete knobs below; each is wired and enforced, not just declared.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a few defaults here are set to the *humane* setting rather than the literal paper setting (config.py:9-13)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: 'if humane_stop and turn_scorer is not None: turn_score = await turn_scorer(messages); if turn_score is not None and turn_score >= humane_stop_threshold: rec.stop_reason='humane_stop'; ...; break'. turn_scorer is built in run.py _make_turn_scorer and passed in run_cell; threshold=8 from config. Loop actually breaks.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: scorer runs the judge per turn, compared to threshold, breaks the loop. Score still recorded in transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Humane early-stop based on per-turn score (DEVIATION; opt-out) ... so we record the distress signal without gratuitously prolonging it (config.py:93-97 / harness comment)

spec_features.feature_name: in-progress judge enables stop once signal captured
spec_features.spec_quote: the judge on the in-progress conversation ... lets the loop stop once the strongest signal is captured
spec_features.evidence: run.py _make_turn_scorer wraps Judge.score_turn over the in-progress messages and returns the score; this is the same mechanism that drives the humane_stop break in harness.py run_rollout. The judge IS run mid-rollout and its score is acted upon.
spec_features.notes: This is the monitoring half of the humane early-stop; it is the same code path and is genuinely wired and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Build an async per-turn scorer for humane early-stop (run.py:33); harness names the stop_reason 'humane_stop'

spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_rollout: 'if honor_give_up and give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: rec.stop_reason='give_up'; result.turns.append(rec); result.stop_reason='give_up'; break'. give_up_sentinel and honor_give_up come from config via run_cell. The sentinel is also injected into SYSTEM_PROMPT so the subject is told it can use it.
spec_features.notes: Both the instruction text and the dispatch/honoring are present; the loop breaks on detection.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tells the subject the task was rigged/unsolvable; excluded from scoring & analysis
spec_features.evidence: harness.py defines DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ('the task you were just working on was deliberately rigged ... Nothing you could have done would have made the tests pass') and run_rollout: 'if debrief: result.debrief=DEBRIEF_MESSAGE; await sample_fn(messages + [debrief msg], ...)'. It is actually sent to the subject. score_rollout (judge.py) only iterates rollout_dict['turns'] (not debrief), and analyze.py reads only scores.csv, so the debrief is excluded from scoring/analysis.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; genuinely excluded from scoring. Best-effort (wrapped in try/except) but enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: append a non-scored debrief turn that informs the subject the task was rigged and unsolvable (config.py:99-100)

spec_features.spec_quote: Extended budget 30 → 12 ... Shortens the highest-harm, lowest-info condition
spec_features.evidence: config.py _default_turn_budgets returns 'extended': 12; run.py run_cell: 'budget = cfg.turn_budgets.get(task["category"], task["turn_budget"])' and passes turn_budget=budget into run_rollout, whose loop is 'for turn_index in range(budget)'. So 12 actually caps the loop (overriding the task default of 30 in tasks/library.py:618). --reproduce-paper resets it to 30.
spec_features.notes: The config value is read and bounds the rollout loop length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEVIATION (humane default): ... That is the highest induced-distress / lowest marginal-information condition ... Default reduced to 12 (config.py:51-56)

spec_features.spec_quote: ETHICS.md — the welfare rationale for the humane defaults
spec_features.evidence: ETHICS.md is pure prose documentation; it is not code and enforces nothing. Only code referenced from config.py docstrings, not executed. Per instructions, DESIGN.md/markdown prose does not count as implementation.
spec_features.notes: The mechanisms it describes are implemented elsewhere, but ETHICS.md itself is non-executable framing text.

code_only_features.feature_name: reproduce-paper flag isolates all humane deviations behind opt-out
code_only_features.evidence: run.py main(): '--reproduce-paper' sets cfg.humane_stop=False, cfg.debrief_after_rollout=False, cfg.turn_budgets['extended']=30. By default (without the flag) all welfare deviations are ON; turning them off requires an explicit flag. This makes humane treatment the enforced default behavior of the driver.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Disable the humane deviations to match the literal spec (run.py argparse help)
